g.title: BGS_QSP
g.text: Bartter & Gitelman Syndrome — QSP Mechanistic Map
Salt-Losing Tubulopathies: nephron-segment transport · macula densa NaCl sensing · COX-2/PGE
amplification · RAAS · divalent cation handling · drug PK/PD · clinical endpoints
lesion POSITION relative to the macula densa — not lesion identity — sets the PGE
phenotype, the SIGN of urinary calcium, and whether COX inhibition works.
FTAL = fractional thick-ascending-limb NaCl transport capacity · FDCT = fractional distal-convoluted-tubule NCC capacity

Bartter I-V · Gitelman · phenocopies. Each gene maps onto a single point in the TAL/DCT transport chain.

g.title: cluster_md
g.text: 5. Macula Densa and Juxtaglomerular Apparatus — where POSITION becomes PHENOTYPE
The macula densa sits at the END of the TAL. A TAL lesion blinds it; a DCT lesion does not. This one fact generates the whole Bartter/Gitelman divergence.

g.title: cluster_raas
g.text: Secondary hyperreninaemic hyperaldosteronism WITHOUT hypertension — the diagnostic signature of a salt-wasting lesion.

g.title: cluster_lytes
g.text: 7. Systemic Electrolytes and Acid-Base — the shared final common path
Hypokalaemic hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis is common to BOTH syndromes; magnesium and calcium are what separate them.

g.title: cluster_renal
g.text: 10. Renal Structural Progression — the Bartter-specific long-term risk
Hypercalciuria is what converts a lifelong electrolyte disorder into progressive CKD; Gitelman rarely does this.

g.title: cluster_antenatal
g.text: Fetal polyuria is the earliest reading of a TAL lesion — and MAGED2 disease reverses itself.

g.title: cluster_drug
g.text: 12. Therapeutics — PK and Mechanism of Action
No disease-specific drug exists. Every agent below is a repurposed physiological counter-move.
